title: Sensors, actuators, and power safety

spans.text: LESSON PURPOSE

Goal: apply “Sensors, actuators, and power safety” to a real program or device. The key principle is: GPIO should drive loads only within documented current limits. In a project, follow this guidance: Verify supply voltage, current budget, and grounding before powering the circuit.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
EXAMPLE CODE
EXPECTED RESULT
The built-in LED is on when the analog reading is greater than 500; sensor and ADC values depend on hardware.
CORE EXPLANATION
Sensors measure physical quantities; actuators turn electricity into motion, light, or sound. Do not drive motors or relays directly from GPIO; use suitable drivers and protection.
IMPORTANT LINE BREAKDOWN
Key line:
int reading = analogRead(sensorPin);

What it does: GPIO should drive loads only within documented current limits.
Why it is used: Verify supply voltage, current budget, and grounding before powering the circuit.
If omitted or changed: Choose parts using recommended operating conditions, not absolute maximum ratings.

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: Mains voltage is hazardous; use current-limited low-voltage supplies for beginner projects.
